assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald-Hartwig amination) is a general method that turned aryl C-N bond formation from a harsh, narrow-scope problem into a routine step. It is ubiquitous in medicinal chemistry and process chemistry and rests on a clear mechanistic picture and rationally designed ligand families. In terms of what changed how chemists everywhere build bonds, it is the strongest case on the list.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled versions in the mid-1990s and then drove the scope and ligand generations. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precursor but required stoichiometric tin reagents, so I would not put him in the prize unless the committee wanted a historical anchor. Two laureates is a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent use in industry and academia, with a very large literature and no stability concerns. Recognition is, if anything, overdue, and it sits comfortably after the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views it as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
How much weight to give Kosugi's precursor tin-amide chemistry; I am relying on memory of the literature and have not verified the details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a new mode of reactivity, with single-electron radical pathways under mild conditions, and enabled previously difficult bond constructions including in late-stage functionalization and dual catalysis with transition metals. The adoption in synthesis labs and pharmaceutical discovery is very broad, and it is conceptually simple: a photocatalyst turns light into redox power.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 papers from MacMillan (with Nicewicz) and Yoon, and Stephenson's 2009 work, are the usual founding trio, with Yoon often credited for the photochemical cycloadditions. MacMillan already has a 2021 prize, which complicates his inclusion but does not remove his decisive role. Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre made important contributions, so credit is genuinely diffuse and a three-person cut will leave out serious contributors.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and heavy adoption within about 15 years. The field is still evolving, which makes it somewhat younger than the cross-coupling cases, though the core is stable.
uncertainties: Whether MacMillan's earlier prize weighs against him.
Early photochemistry precedents (Kellogg, Fukuzumi, Deronzier and others) complicate priority; I cannot verify the details from this packet.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization lets chemists treat ubiquitous C-H bonds as reactive handles, shortening syntheses, which is the efficiency argument I care most about. Ligand-controlled Pd catalysis (Yu), Ir-catalyzed borylation (Hartwig, Smith) and directed Pd(II)/Pd(IV) chemistry (Sanford, Daugulis) are real, widely used methods with applications in total synthesis and late-stage diversification.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the main problem. The field has several parallel streams (directing groups, ligand acceleration, borylation, Pd(II)/Pd(IV)), and a three-person cut can only capture part of it. Yu for ligand-enabled and template-controlled selectivity, Sanford for the mechanistic and catalytic foundation, and Hartwig for borylation is a defensible but not obviously fair configuration. Hartwig also appears in B057, which could matter for portfolio balance.
assessment.maturity: Methods are used widely but are still being expanded, and industrial uptake outside borylation is more modest than for cross-coupling. Moderately mature, probably a little early.
uncertainties: Practical generality of directed C-H functionalization beyond specialist labs versus the headline claims; I have not verified the extent of industrial use.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made chemical synthesis of proteins practical by joining unprotected peptide segments chemoselectively at a cysteine. It provides total chemical synthesis of proteins, semisynthesis with expressed protein ligation, and site-specific modification, and the chemical idea is simple and general.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported NCL in 1994, and Muir extended it to expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky contributed to later ligation-desulfurization strategies and glycoprotein synthesis, so credit to him is arguable. Kent, Dawson and Muir is a coherent and fairly tight trio.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use and a stable body of work, including synthetic proteins and chemically modified histones. Timely and mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct in impact from the 1984 Merrifield solid-phase peptide synthesis prize.
Danishefsky's and Brik's later contributions might be underweighted by a three-person cut.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another in genomic DNA without double-strand cleavage, which is a new chemical concept (deaminase fused to a programmable DNA-binding protein) with clear therapeutic potential and clinical translation under way. From my perspective the chemical novelty is the engineered deamination chemistry, and that is real, though the platform builds on CRISPR, which was already recognized in 2020.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the work and Komor and Gaudelli were the lead authors of the cytosine and adenine base editors. A prize configuration of Liu alone is possible, and including the two trainees is unusual for the Nobel but is supported by the supplied credit. Kondo and Nishida's parallel cytidine deaminase work complicates a clean assignment.
assessment.maturity: About a decade old, with first clinical results emerging. Impact is high but long-term safety and efficacy are still being established, so this is maturing rather than mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges that this adds enough beyond the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Clinical durability and off-target effects are not settled; I cannot verify the current clinical status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation, with heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glue degraders, introduced a new pharmacological modality: using small molecules to recruit E3 ligases and destroy proteins. The medicinal chemistry rationale is elegant, many compounds are in the clinic, and thalidomide analogue mechanisms were clarified as molecular glues.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept in 2001, and Ciulli contributed structure-guided VHL ligands and mechanism. The molecular glue stream (Handa, Ito, Gray and others) means the supplied credit contains a compound discovery, and a fair trio would not cover everything. Allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Strong conceptual confirmation, but clinical validation is still in progress, so recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be recognized together or separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes changed the view of a supposedly transient species and gave the field N-heterocyclic carbenes as ligands (key to modern metathesis and cross-coupling catalysts) and as organocatalysts. The conceptual shift was large and the downstream uses are broad across catalysis and main-group chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand isolated the first stable phosphinocarbene in 1988 and Arduengo the crystalline imidazol-2-ylidene in 1991, so both have legitimate priority claims. Nolan, Rovis and Bode drove applications in catalysis, but they are further downstream.
assessment.maturity: Well over thirty years of confirmation and use, so it is clearly mature.
uncertainties: Some of the practical impact is channeled through other, already recognized, catalysis prizes.
Relative priority between Bertrand's carbene and Arduengo's NHC could be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave controlled radical polymerization with good control over molecular weight, architecture and end groups using simple transition-metal catalysis. It is used widely for well-defined polymers and materials, and it applies the catalytic logic that organic chemists recognize.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto reported the approach independently in 1995, with Wang as a coauthor on the Matyjaszewski paper. Matyjaszewski plus Sawamoto is the natural pair. RAFT and nitroxide-mediated polymerization are competing controlled radical methods, which could argue for treating the field together.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years old and widely commercialized, with a stable mechanism and extensive independent confirmation.
uncertainties: Polymer chemistry sits outside my own area, so I am less able to judge relative importance.
Overlap with RAFT and other controlled radical methods complicates the case for singling out ATRP.
